newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Former rebel chief to help Philippine peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Former rebel chief to help Philippine peace talks.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Saturday authorised Moslem regional governor Nur Misuari, a former rebel chief, to help break the deadlock in talks with a Moslem separatist group.
A statement from the presidential palace said Misuari has been directed to initiate contact with the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF).
Misuari is chairman of the MNLF. Last September he signed a peace agreement with Manila, formally ending a 24-year MNLF-led revolt for Moslem self-rule in the southern Mindanao region.
Shortly afterwards, he was elected as governor of a semi-autonomous Moslem region comprising four provinces.
The MILF was not party to the MNLF peace deal but has begun separate peace talks with the government.
Resumption of talks last weekend, however, was deferred after two weeks of fighting between the military and the guerrillas that left more than 80 people dead.

The latest clash was an attack by MILF rebels on an army camp in the southern province of Maguindanao early on Saturday morning. Seven rebels died and six people were wounded in the ensuing skirmish, the military said.
The MILF, estimated to have 8,000 armed activists, is battling for independence for Mindanao, the ancestral Moslem homeland in a predominantly Christian country.
The palace statement said Misuari attended a meeting with top officials led by Defence Secretary Renato de Villa to discuss peace efforts in Mindanao.
